item.text:
**1B.7 Research Note: Abiy Ahmed in 2024**

**Read:** I found mixed evidence. There is some 2024 institutional-building around disaster response and civilian nuclear cooperation, but the stronger security-side evidence points toward centralized, politically controlled security mechanisms rather than insulated expert institutions. I found no direct 2024 evidence that Abiy built a professional, independent nuclear/security advisory system.

| Date | Title | Publisher | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-04-26 | Commission Revamping Disaster Response Works to Address Humanitarian Needs | ENA English | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4358046 | Ethiopia’s Disaster Risk Management Commission said it was overhauling structure, policy, staffing, and technology to improve emergency management and response capacity. This is the strongest positive evidence that Abiy’s government invested in risk-reducing institutions rather than ad hoc control. | 1B.7, 1B.3 |
| 2024-07-05 | Officials said the newly ratified disaster-risk policy would help Ethiopia mitigate and respond to natural and manmade calamities using its own resources, with a new structure for the commission. | ENA English | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4724392 | The government framed the new disaster-risk policy as a way to build preventive and response capacity from within state institutions. This supports a technocratic, institution-building interpretation. | 1B.7, 1B.3 |
| 2024-08-17 | Council Vows to Strengthen Disaster Emergency Response Activities in Ethiopia | ENA English | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4989768 | The disaster-risk council said Ethiopia needed a more effective emergency-preparedness system and stronger prevention and information-sharing after landslides and floods. This is further evidence of investment in risk-reduction expertise and procedures. | 1B.7, 1B.3 |
| 2024-07-01 | Discussion Held with CNNC on Potential Collaboration in Nuclear Energy in Ethiopia | ENA English | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4693757 | Ethiopian officials discussed peaceful nuclear cooperation, including infrastructure development and human-resource training for a future nuclear program. This is positive, but only indirect, evidence of building technical expertise around a sensitive domain. | 1B.7, 1B.4, 1B.5 |
| 2024-09-21 | Ethiopia to Chair AFRA for One Year | ENA English | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5179100 | Ethiopia took over chairmanship of AFRA, a framework for peaceful nuclear science and technology in Africa. That supports a reading of engagement with expert nuclear institutions rather than purely ideological control. | 1B.7, 1B.4, 1B.5 |
| 2024-02-23 | Special report | In Ethiopia, secret committee ‘orders killings and arrests to crush rebels’ | Times LIVE, reporting Reuters investigation | https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/africa/2024-02-23-special-report-in-ethiopia-secret-committee-orders-killings-and-arrests-to-crush-rebels/ | Reuters reported a secretive “Koree Nageenyaa” security committee in Oromia that allegedly ordered killings and arrests to crush dissent. This is strong negative evidence: security decisions were tied to a covert, politically aligned apparatus, not transparent expert institutions. | 1B.7, 1B.5, 7A.* |
| 2024-02-02 | Ethiopia extends state of emergency in Amhara | Reuters via KELO | https://kelo.com/2024/02/02/ethiopia-extends-state-of-emergency-in-amhara/ | Parliament extended emergency rule amid insurgency and hundreds of deaths. This indicates reliance on emergency coercive structures rather than normal risk-governance institutions. | 1B.7, 7A.* |
| 2024-11-03 | Details of State of Emergency Declared by Gov't of Ethiopia | ENA English | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/en_30124 | The proclamation centralized coercive authority and authorized an operation command to issue directives. That cuts against independent, expertise-based risk governance and suggests concentration of decision-making power. | 1B.7, 7A.* |
| 2024-06-18 | Ethiopia: Halt Crackdown Against Human Rights Groups | Human Rights Watch | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/18/ethiopia-halt-crackdown-against-human-rights-groups | HRW said security and intelligence personnel followed, intimidated, and threatened human-rights workers. This supports the view that security institutions were used for control and suppression, not insulated expert judgment. | 1B.7, 7A.* |
| 2024-07-04 | Ethiopia's Abiy says rights body 'hijacked' by foreigners | AFP via EWN | https://www.ewn.co.za/2024/07/04/ethiopias-abiy-says-rights-body-hijacked-by-foreigners | Abiy’s rhetoric toward oversight institutions was hostile and delegitimizing. That is consistent with surrounding sensitive decisions with loyalists or ideologues rather than independent expertise. | 1B.7, 7A.* |

**Search gap**

- I searched directly for 2024 evidence on technocrats, security appointments, institutional reform, and nuclear/security decision-making.
- I did not find a direct source showing Abiy created an expert-led nuclear-security council, independent advisory structure, or formal safeguards body.
- I also did not find a direct source proving the opposite in a nuclear-specific sense.
- So the best-supported reading is indirect: some real institution-building in disaster response and peaceful nuclear cooperation, but stronger evidence of centralized and politicized security governance.

**Bottom line**

- Positive side: there was visible investment in disaster-risk institutions and civilian nuclear capacity-building.
- Negative side: core security governance still looked centralized, emergency-based, and politically controlled.
- Overall: mixed evidence, leaning negative on the specific question of whether he privileged independent expertise over loyalist-driven security control.
